text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad has directed state chief ministers to keep a close check on entertainment and gaming outlets. The order was given after Mahathir was briefed on the country's social situation.

-- State power firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd will take steps to reduce the 500 million ringgit worth of electricity it loses annually, its executive chairman Ahmad Tajuddin Ali said. He said the loss, estimated at 15 percent of the company's total power production, was excessive.

-- The Malaysia government has focussed its energies to fight three perils -- growing drug abuse, rising number of illegal immigrants and social problems -- now facing the country. Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob said all security agencies and local governments had been directed to go all out to resolve them.

-- The Cabinet has decided to make Malaysian waters off limits in the transhipment of logs from neighbouring countries, which have banned the export of logs. The decision comes in the wake of rampant log smuggling activities in eastern Sabah state.
